info.title: TG-Sentry protection API
info.description: #13 protection mutations use the admin cookie and existing CSRF/origin boundary; #15 GET /api/v1/client/bundle uses enrolled-device bearer auth. All/tag/agent policies are additive (any matching tag); block > alert > log-only; global and #55 node bindings cannot be weakened. Agent IDs mean enrolled client node IDs, never untrusted session IDs. Templates select existing GET /api/v1/rules detector IDs, snapshotted at review (no new detectors). Rule definitions are server-owned and not accepted in requests. Policy template references follow latest published template. Every create/update/delete/tag change requires review then explicit confirmation, with the same global If-Match ETag; unrelated protection changes invalidate reviews. Review returns field diff, affected policies/agents, overlaps, and protection-removal warning; confirmDowngrade=true required when flagged. In-use template deletion returns bound policy IDs in error. No automatic retry; creation is not retry-safe. Existing centralized evaluator applies published config on the next submission; the command bridge now conditionally fetches signed bundles per hook (#15); scheduled daemon polling/sync progress and per-policy transport-failure defaults remain deferred. Names <=200 bytes (existing rule limit), tags <=120 bytes (existing enrollment name limit), <=10 tags (FEATURE-INVENTORY.md:50). Errors reuse existing {error:string} envelope. Read empty lists are [], tags are []. Standards: RFC 9110 section 13.1.1; RFC 6585 section 3; XACML 3.0 Appendix C deny-overrides. Precedents: internal/core/policy_bindings.go, DECISIONS #19, docs/design/CONSOLE-DESIGN.md F2/F3. All future agents are included for all bindings. Detector-definition changes also appear in the diff. Any retained detector change to matcher, target, tool, field or pattern conservatively requires downgrade acknowledgement. Create reviews assign the new opaque resourceId. DELETE requests carry the confirmation JSON body. No review expiry is imposed; old revisions cannot publish. M1 single-writer aggregate follows store_database.go; split/index only when measured scale requires it.

post.description: #40 S1 contract freeze; RFC 8628 sections 3.1/3.2. Unauthenticated bootstrap exception, exact method+path only (no auth-prefix exemption). UTF-8 application/x-www-form-urlencoded. The fixed nonsecret client_id=aegishook (named local exception, #40 S3 lead disposition: CLI binary/module name; public CLI identification precedent, RFC 8628 section 3.1/RFC 6749 section 2.1) is distinct from the console OIDC client ID; there is no CLI client secret. Missing/unknown client_id returns HTTP 400 invalid_client (RFC 6749 section 5.2); duplicate parameters return invalid_request. Absent/empty scope is accepted; any nonempty scope returns invalid_scope because no named scope is exposed. name/platform are TG-Sentry extensions validated and bound to the grant at creation (descriptive, never attestation); scope is limited to existing endpoint-device access. Duplicate parameters are rejected, empty values are omitted, unrecognised parameters are ignored (section 3.1). verification_uri is generated from configured server identity, never Host/forwarded headers; verification_uri_complete is intentionally omitted in this version (section 3.2.1 unused). expires_in 900 s (GitHub device flow, Step 1: default 900 s/15 min); interval 5 s (section 3.2). device_code is 256 random bits (ID()+ID(), internal/core/client_requests.go:89); user_code is 8 characters from the section 6.1 alphabet BCDFGHJKLMNPQRSTVWXZ displayed XXXX-XXXX, selected with unbiased cryptography. Admission reuses the 5/256 per-source/global caps shared with the legacy request flow (client_requests.go:77-90). Production requires TLS; loopback HTTP is a documented development/test exception. User-code submission is throttled at 50 per hour per application, counting unsuccessful guesses (GitHub device flow, rate limits).

400.description: Malformed or unsupported request; RFC 6749 section 5.2 error body (invalid_request, invalid_scope).

500.description: Store unavailable; generic OAuth error only.

post.summary: Poll the device-authorization grant for a token
post.description: #40 S1 contract freeze; RFC 8628 sections 3.4/3.5 and RFC 6749 section 5.2. Form-encoded POST only: no GET polling, no user code in the token request, no device code in browser URLs. Grant type urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code. The fixed nonsecret client_id=aegishook (named local exception, #40 S3 lead disposition: CLI binary/module name, RFC 8628 section 3.1/RFC 6749 section 2.1 public-client precedent) is validated identically to device-authorization; missing/unknown client_id returns HTTP 400 invalid_client (RFC 6749 section 5.2), duplicate parameters return invalid_request. The token endpoint ignores unrecognized request parameters including scope (RFC 6749 section 3.2; RFC 8628 section 3.4 defines no token-request scope); scope validation applies only to device-authorization. Only authorization_pending and slow_down are nonterminal; slow_down adds 5 s cumulatively to the required interval (section 3.5), and the client applies exponential timeout backoff while retaining the original expiry deadline. Any other OAuth error is terminal and never auto-starts a new grant. Success returns the existing revocable device bearer as access_token with token_type Bearer (RFC 6749 section 5.1) plus the documented TG-Sentry bootstrap extensions nodeId, bundlePublicKey and bundleTrust (ClientConnection shapes). No refresh token; device-token lifetime is revocation-based and is not the grant expires_in. On success the poll atomically consumes the approved grant, issues the credential and writes the issuance audit using the approving actor saved at decision time (RFC 8628 section 3.5). Server enforces the interval; concurrent successful polls issue at most one credential. Errors are RFC 6749 section 5.2 bodies. #72 S1: in that same transaction copy the grant confirmed principal to immutable ClientNode.associatedUser, or leave it null when unassociated. Retain only the node association after redemption; no identity fields on Instance/Review or additional token-response fields. Failed issuance/audit rolls back both consumption and association.

200.description: Access token (RFC 6749 section 5.1) plus TG-Sentry enrollment bootstrap extensions.

400.description: RFC 6749 section 5.2 error body. Nonterminal: authorization_pending, slow_down. Terminal (RFC 8628 section 3.5): access_denied, expired_token, invalid_grant. Malformed/unsupported: invalid_request, unsupported_grant_type.

500.description: Store unavailable; generic OAuth error only.

post.summary: Inspect a submitted user code (human admin)
post.description: #40 S1 contract freeze. Human-admin cookie session only; readonly, auditor, kind:cli, hook tokens and device credentials are denied (RFC 8628 section 3.3; existing RBAC). GET/navigation never approves, and there is no automatic approval. Returns the grant's descriptive device name/platform and trusted-proxy-resolved request source; endpoint-supplied metadata is descriptive, not attestation. The submitted code counts against the 50/hour application throttle, including unsuccessful guesses. #72 S1: returns optional confirmed associatedUser separately from the approving Actor and a grant-specific ETag. Null permits explicit unassociated approval; it never implies the admin is the user.

ETag.description: Strong grant ETag covering reviewed device details, lifecycle and confirmed associatedUser (including null); confirmation changes it. RFC 9110 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-8.8.3.

post.summary: Approve or deny a device grant (human admin)
post.description: #40 S1 contract freeze. Human-admin cookie session only; the loopback kind:cli session cannot approve even with an admin role (D2; existing RBAC). Explicit approve/deny only; no automatic approval from an existing login. This endpoint ONLY records the approve/deny decision and the authenticated human actor (iss, sub); it does NOT consume the grant and does NOT issue any credential. The successful device-token poll atomically consumes the approved grant, issues at most one credential and writes the issuance audit using the approving actor saved at decision time (RFC 8628 section 3.5; mirrors the approve/redeem split at internal/core/client_requests.go:97-147). Only the digest of the issued bearer is persisted, so a lost token response cannot be replayed from a hash-only store (one-time issuance, not exactly-once delivery). #72 S1: association, when selected, must be explicitly confirmed before decision and cannot change afterwards. Unassociated approval remains available. Atomically require the ETag from admin lookup so approval matches the reviewed association; concurrent confirmation invalidates stale approval. RFC 9110 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-13.1.1; missing precondition follows RFC 6585 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6585.html#section-3. No automatic retry.

409.description: Grant already decided; re-deciding is refused. Consumption and credential issuance happen only at the device-token poll.

412.description: Stale reviewed grant/association or weak tag; reload for human review, never retry automatically.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: Reuse protection conditional writes, but compare to this grant ETag, not the global protection revision. At least one strong tag in the entity-tag list must equal the reviewed current grant ETag; stale or weak tags return 412, missing returns 428. Wildcard is intentionally disallowed. RFC 9110 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-13.1.1.

post.summary: Begin end-user OIDC association for a pending user code
post.description: #72 S1 docs-only contract. Exact-method/path bootstrap exception permits only initiation, never grant decision or identity writes. Same-origin mutation checks and #40 user-code expiry/throttle apply, including unsuccessful guesses; no new limits. Resolve a pending grant and bind it in server-owned state in this browser before redirecting through existing GET /api/v1/auth/login and /api/v1/auth/callback. Existing issuer/client, signature, audience/azp, nonce, PKCE, state/cookie and safe-redirect checks remain; callback query parameters cannot select the admission exception or swap the grant. No identity fields in the body; no automatic association from a console session. Roleless employees may receive the existing kind:human cookie session only for the bound association continuation, without a role; normal login still returns 403 no_role. OIDC/session/grant deadlines are reused and grant life is never extended. RFC 8628 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8628.html#section-3.3; Okta https://developer.okta.com/docs/guides/device-authorization-grant/main/#request-access-id-and-refresh-tokens; Entra https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/v2-oauth2-device-code#authenticating-the-user; OIDC Core https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html#IDTokenValidation; RFC 7636 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7636.html#section-4.6.

302.description: Browser navigation through existing OIDC login; server-owned state/cookie carries the grant binding. No user association yet.

Location.description: Same-origin existing /api/v1/auth/login; no device code or bearer in the URL.

409.description: Grant already confirmed or decided; no replacement/restart of association.

get.summary: Review the verified account and bound device before association
get.description: #72 S1. Existing human cookie plus server-owned pending-grant continuation required, including a roleless human admitted solely for this grant. No caller-selected grant ID. Only the existing verified OIDC callback supplies user; GET and callback bind nothing. No /me, management, audit, lookup or decision permission is added to roleless sessions. Expired/decided/replayed continuation fails closed; reuse existing deadlines. Account identity follows OIDC Core https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html#ClaimStability.

200.description: Verified candidate user and descriptive device; explicit POST still required.

403.description: Missing/wrong grant-bound continuation, nonhuman credential or origin denied.

409.description: Association confirmed or grant already decided; continuation no longer usable.

post.summary: Explicitly confirm this verified account for the bound device grant
post.description: #72 S1. Existing human cookie plus server-owned grant continuation; normal console login alone is insufficient. Same-origin mutation checks apply. Only {confirm:true}; issuer/subject/name/grantId and other fields are rejected. Resolve grant and verified candidate identity from server state, never browser/admin strings. Atomically confirm only while pending, unexpired and not yet associated; confirmed identity is immutable, competing claims/replays/decided grants fail closed. Callback/GET never confirms. The approving Actor stays separate; confirmation neither approves nor issues a credential. No two-person rule. Reuse existing OIDC/session and original #40 expiry/throttle. RFC 8628 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8628.html#section-3.3; OIDC Core https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html#ClaimStability.

200.description: Confirmed association awaiting separate admin decision; invalidate this continuation.

ETag.description: Strong grant ETag covering reviewed device details, lifecycle and confirmed associatedUser (including null); confirmation changes it. RFC 9110 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-8.8.3.

403.description: Wrong/missing continuation, nonhuman credential or origin denied.

409.description: Confirmed association cannot be replaced; competing/replayed confirmation or decided grant.

get.summary: List metadata-only grouped session audit summaries
get.description: #16 existing route; #72 S1 adds users derived from review→instance→node and zero-call instances→node, not activity-row identity snapshots. Human admin/auditor/readonly may read metadata; local CLI, hook/device bearers and roleless association continuations cannot. Exact userIssuer+userSubject pair must both be supplied nonempty or both absent; duplicate values are rejected. Preserve decoded strings exactly, without trimming, case folding, issuer normalization, name/email matching or mixing pairs from different nodes (OIDC Core https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html#ClaimStability). Tenant-scoped parameterized matching selects grouped sessions containing a node with that association before count/pagination, returning all users/agents/devices in the group. It does not prove the selected person executed every call. Revoked-node association remains visible; legacy/unassociated/missing nodes and unresolvable orphan reviews are unassociated, with no backfill. user:null/userState:unassociated remain deprecated compatibility constants; users/devices drive new display and hasUnassociatedActivity flags any contributing review without an associated user. No OCSF actor.user. Existing ordering/time semantics remain (ARCHITECTURE #16); no raw content or credentials.

parameters.name: userIssuer
parameters.description: Exact verified issuer; requires userSubject. Both absent means no user filter; blank/incomplete/duplicate pair returns 400.

parameters.name: userSubject
parameters.description: Exact verified subject under userIssuer, matched on the same node association. No name/email search.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Existing #16 UTC date-only or RFC3339/Nano lower bound, inclusive.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Existing #16 date-only upper bound advances to following UTC midnight; timestamp upper bound is exclusive.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Existing #16 positive page and integer/offset-overflow validation.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Existing #16 /calls bounds, not a new numeric profile.

200.description: Filtered total and descending sessionTime/sessionId page; empty items/users are [].

get.summary: Fetch a signed revisioned effective-policy bundle
get.description: #15/#65. Enrolled device identity is server-derived. ETag/If-None-Match per OPA and RFC 9110 sections 13.1.2/15.4.5. Revoked devices are rejected before conditional handling. The command bridge fetches per hook under its existing deadline; no daemon timer exists. Verify Ed25519 over exact decoded payload bytes under the current trusted key set, bootstrapped by authenticated enrollment bundleTrust (legacy omission implies v1 containing bundlePublicKey). keyId is an unsigned selection hint; when absent, trial-verify the current trusted keys. TG-Trust-Version is present on 200 and 304 so key-only rotation remains observable without changing the payload ETag. If trust is newer or keyId is unknown, retrieve each successive /api/v1/client/keys/{version}, verifying version N+1 under both the previous and new sets and persisting each accepted record (TUF section 5.3). Require nondecreasing policy revision and identical bytes at equal revision (TUF section 5.4.3). Network bundles must verify under the current trust record; retain the prior verified private cache on failure, but cached rules cannot allow offline execution. No expiry; compromised-key recovery requires re-enrollment, not cross-signing.

parameters.name: If-None-Match
parameters.description: Previously verified bundle ETag. Omit when the cached signer is no longer in the current trust record to obtain a newly signed 200. GET weak comparison, lists and wildcard are supported.

200.description: Signed bundle. JSON byte strings use base64; this is not OPA wire format.

ETag.description: Strong quoted SHA-256 of exact decoded payload bytes (RFC 9110 section 8.8.3). Includes revision and node identity.

TG-Trust-Version.description: Current committed trust-record version, including on 304 for key-only changes. Header name is the named local exception in issue #65 section 9.3.

304.description: No body. Only valid against an already verified matching cache.

ETag.description: Strong quoted SHA-256 of exact decoded payload bytes (RFC 9110 section 8.8.3). Includes revision and node identity.

TG-Trust-Version.description: Current committed trust-record version, including on 304 for key-only changes. Header name is the named local exception in issue #65 section 9.3.

503.description: Policy or store unavailable; preserve trusted cache and apply failure default.

get.summary: Fetch one signed public trust record
get.description: Issue #65 section 3.6; TUF section 5.3 per-version retrieval. Requires enrolled-device bearer authentication and the existing client source-IP/origin restrictions, exactly like /api/v1/client/bundle; admin cookies and legacy shared HookToken do not authorize this route. Each response is one committed public record, never private signing material. Fetch successive versions without skipping, verify both previous and new trust sets, and persist each accepted record before fetching the next. Unknown versions return 404. Compromised-key recovery requires re-enrollment.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: Positive trust-record version, retrieved in N+1 order.

200.description: One signed trust record, within the existing 2 MiB response budget. Byte strings are base64; this is not TUF wire format.

503.description: Trust record unavailable; preserve trusted state and apply failure default.

get.description: Issue #48 Slice 1: enrolled-device whitelist resource only; runtime audit/content suppression is not implemented in this slice. Agent IDs select all protected agents on those enrolled devices, following #44; users await #72. Readonly sessions may read; only human admins may review and publish. Creation/enabling or enabled subject changes require recording-loss acknowledgement (confirmDowngrade=true); protection and risk reporting are not disabled. Global ETag/If-Match, strict JSON and atomic actor-attributed protection.log-whitelist.publish audit reuse the ACL resource. Missing/empty collection is empty, no virtual default. Unknown node references return 404; revoked nodes return 400 and are rechecked at confirmation. IDs and updatedAt are server-owned. Whitelist subjects are not distributed in endpoint bundles.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: Entity-tag list per RFC 9110 sections 8.8.3 and 13.1.1. At least one strong tag must equal the current global ETag (for example "0"); otherwise 412. Weak tags do not match. Wildcard is intentionally disallowed; missing If-Match returns 428.

post.description: Admin-only tenant singleton. Uses the existing protection review/confirm flow and global If-Match; unknown fields, non-integer or overflowing intervals and negative intervals are rejected. Omitted scalar fields use Go zero values; false or zero disables discovery. JSON null bodies and null scalar values are rejected with a static protection-invalid error. The exact zero value (false, 0), including {}, normalizes to absence before diffing; when already absent it has no reviewable changes (400) and does not advance any revision. Nonzero settings are retained even when scanning is disabled.

discovery.description: Null when the exact zero value cleared discovery from the protection state and bundle.

put.description: Admin-only confirmation of the reviewed discovery settings; atomically publishes protection state, audit and bundle revision. No direct settings write and no discovery-specific downgrade rule.

deviceCredential.description: Existing per-device credential from authenticated enrollment; not an admin cookie or legacy shared HookToken.

Error409.description: Missing review, downgrade acknowledgement, or template in use

Error412.description: Stale global revision or stale review; retain draft, never retry automatically

SupplyChainFamily.description: Existing #42 asset families; admission does not expand capture or enforcement coverage.

SupplyChainSubjectDigest.description: Exact #42 SupplyChainSubject.Digest over complete captured membership; no name, path, inventory ID, wildcard or alternate hashing format.

Actor.description: Existing core.Actor attribution. Server-owned authenticated context, never admission request input.

name.description: Display-only; nonblank and at most 200 UTF-8 bytes (existing validProtectionName boundary), not a character maxLength.

AdmittedAsset.description: #43 S1 contract only; management routes arrive in S3. Tenant-wide human-admin exception for any scanner grade. Enabled entries match only the server tenant, family and byte-exact subject digest. Family/digest/source are immutable; changed bytes require a new admission. Suppresses only the supply-chain restriction, never a terminal approve or a clean-scan claim; other checks remain authoritative. No expiry or second approver. Precedents: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/indicator-file#policy-conflict-handling-for-file-indicators and https://northpole.dev/features/binary-authorization/.

name.description: Nonblank, at most 200 UTF-8 bytes (existing validProtectionName boundary).

sourceSnapshotId.description: Existing trusted complete #42 capture; the server resolves its family and validates its subject, never a browser-supplied manifest.

expectedSubjectDigest.description: Exact digest the operator reviewed; refuse a stale source rather than admitting changed bytes.

AdmittedAssetCreateInput.description: Creation review input, not direct publication. Actor, tenant, IDs and timestamps are server-owned. Scan cleanliness is not required. Confirmation reuses the existing Confirm contract.

name.description: Nonblank, at most 200 UTF-8 bytes (existing validProtectionName boundary).

AdmittedAssetUpdateInput.description: Replacement metadata review input; no family, digest or source mutation. Omitted description/enabled use empty/false, matching existing ACL conventions. Removal is a separate reviewed action, not identity editing.

payload.description: Exact compact UTF-8 JSON TrustRecord bytes, signed before envelope encoding.

signatures.description: Distinct keyId entries; at least one valid signature from each of previous and new key sets. At most four distinct signatures from their union (issue #65 section 3.2, internal/core/policy_trust.go).

version.description: Must be exactly N+1 for a chain update.

keys.description: Distinct public keys; two-key bound is a named local exception in issue #65 section 9.2.

publicKey.description: RFC 8032 Ed25519 public key, 32 decoded bytes. keyId must equal its lowercase SHA-256.

signature.description: RFC 8032 Ed25519 signature over exact decoded payload bytes; 64 decoded bytes.

payload.description: Exact UTF-8 JSON bytes described by PolicyBundle; signed before envelope encoding.

signature.description: Detached RFC 8032 Ed25519 signature; 64 decoded bytes.

keyId.description: Optional lowercase SHA-256 of the Ed25519 public key; outside the signed payload. Legacy omission permits trial verification under the current trusted keys.

revision.description: Persisted Settings.Version; changes include rules, Scope bindings, template/policy confirms and tag PUT.

rules.description: Exactly the runtime protectionRules selection, not just global rules. Empty is [], never null.

discovery.description: Optional. Absent leaves pre-discovery payload bytes unchanged; absent, enabled=false or intervalSeconds=0 disables discovery. Published only with an atomic bundle revision advance.

token.description: Private device credential; never place in URLs or logs.

bundlePublicKey.description: RFC 8032 Ed25519 public key, 32 decoded bytes, delivered through authenticated setup-key or approved-request enrollment. The current signer pin is included in bundleTrust. Legacy connections without a pin must re-enroll; connections with a pin but no bundleTrust imply v1 containing that pin. Planned key rotation follows sequential signed trust records; compromised-key recovery requires re-enrollment.

bundleTrust.description: Optional authenticated-enrollment bootstrap snapshot of the current signed trust record; validate the pin belongs to its keys and a new-set signature verifies. Legacy omission implies v1 containing the enrollment pin.

client_id.description: Fixed nonsecret public client identifier, distinct from the console OIDC client ID.

name.description: TG-Sentry extension; device display name bound to the grant. Validated as UTF-8 bytes against the existing 1-120 byte limit (internal/core/client_requests.go:64, client_nodes.go:70), not a character maxLength. Descriptive, not attestation.

platform.description: TG-Sentry extension; endpoint platform, validated and bound to the grant exactly as client/enroll.

scope.description: Optional; limited to existing endpoint-device access. Arbitrary management scopes are rejected.

DeviceAuthorizationRequest.description: Form-encoded (RFC 8628 section 3.1). Duplicate parameters are rejected; empty values are treated as omitted; unrecognised parameters are ignored.

device_code.description: Opaque 256-bit high-entropy code; never displayed and never placed in URLs or browser code. Only its digest is stored.

user_code.description: 8 characters from the RFC 8628 section 6.1 alphabet, displayed XXXX-XXXX; shown in the initiating terminal.

verification_uri.description: Configured server origin + /device; never derived from Host or forwarded headers.

expires_in.description: Grant lifetime in seconds; 900 (GitHub device flow, Step 1).

DeviceTokenRequest.description: Form-encoded (RFC 8628 section 3.4). No GET polling and no user code.

access_token.description: Existing revocable per-device bearer credential; never in URLs or logs. Lifetime is revocation-based, not the grant expires_in.

nodeId.description: TG-Sentry extension; enrolled node ID, the same value the legacy connection returns.

bundlePublicKey.description: TG-Sentry extension; RFC 8032 Ed25519 current-signer pin, as in ClientConnection.

bundleTrust.description: TG-Sentry extension; authenticated-enrollment trust bootstrap, as in ClientConnection.

OAuthError.description: RFC 6749 section 5.2 error body, distinct from the application {error:string} envelope. Values follow RFC 8628 section 3.5.

userCode.description: Displayed code entered for admin lookup or explicit association begin; normalized for case and display hyphen. Counts against #40 submission throttle.

grantId.description: Opaque server-owned grant identifier; not an authorization token.

source.description: Observed request source (trusted-proxy resolved); descriptive, not attestation.

associatedUser.description: #72 S1 server-owned confirmed principal, distinct from the approving Actor. Null before confirmation or for unassociated enrollment; immutable after confirmation/decision.

name.description: Optional display name, existing OIDC name then preferred_username fallback; never an identity key.

AssociatedUser.description: #72 S1 exact server-verified (iss,sub), OIDC Core https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html#ClaimStability. Reuse core.Principal; no source/provenance object, tokens or session IDs. Stored immutably once on ClientNode after grant redemption; absent/null means unassociated.

associatedUser.description: Optional #72 immutable node association. Token-poll redemption alone copies confirmed identity atomically; legacy/setup-key nodes stay unassociated. Revoke/re-enroll to change it; revocation retains historical association.

ClientNode.description: Existing ClientNode metadata (internal/core/client_nodes.go:14-27) plus optional #72 association; no credential hash or new activity-row identity.

DeviceGrantAssociationPreview.description: Server-owned verified OIDC candidate user and pending device; grant.associatedUser remains null until explicit confirmation. No admin-selected identity.

associatedUser.description: Optional node metadata for #72 consumer display; absent/null is unassociated or unresolved. Revoked nodes retain it.

user.description: Existing #16 compatibility constant, always null even with populated users.

userState.description: Existing #16 compatibility constant, not a new associated/mixed state machine; does not summarize users coverage.

users.description: #72 additive collection, [] when no associated contributor; deduplicate by exact issuer+subject, never display name. Derive through contributing instance/node relationships. Return every distinct pair, including in filtered groups; device association is not proof of the executing human.

hasUnassociatedActivity.description: Additive #72 coverage flag: true when at least one contributing review has no associated user - a review on an unassociated node, or an orphan review with no resolvable instance/node, which contributes no devices[] entry. false when every contributing review resolves to an associated node, including a review-less zero-call liveness group. Coverage metadata only, not a count or state enum.

SessionSummary.description: #16 show-all agents/devices precedent; #72 users is a named local collection contract. Legacy/unresolvable orphan contributors remain unassociated; populated users never implies all contributors or calls are associated. No raw content, identity snapshots or OCSF actor.user changes.

LogWhitelistSubject.description: Exact enrolled non-revoked node IDs; all protected agents on each device. No all/tags/users/wildcards; unknown nodes return 404, revoked nodes 400.

LogWhitelistInput.description: For create/update, nonblank name (existing 200-byte limit) and nonempty agents subject required. Enabled defaults false; description defaults empty. For deletion use {"delete":true} at the existing entry review endpoint. No client-owned id or updatedAt.

ACLSubject.description: all has no lists; agents requires distinct enrolled non-revoked node IDs and no tags; tags requires nonempty valid tags and no agentIds. Any matching tag applies.

ACLTarget.description: all has no tools; tools requires nonempty distinct nonblank exact hook tool names. No trimming, case folding, wildcard or namespace interpretation.

ACLInput.description: For create/update, nonblank name, valid subject, effect and target are required; enabled defaults to false. Description defaults to empty. For deletion use {"delete":true} on the resource review endpoint. IDs and updatedAt are server-owned.

TemplateInput.description: For create/update, name and rules/templateIds/scope are required. For deletion use {"delete":true} on the resource review endpoint.

PolicyInput.description: For create/update, name and rules/templateIds/scope are required. For deletion use {"delete":true} on the resource review endpoint.

DiscoveryPolicy.description: Discovery requires enabled=true and intervalSeconds>0. Omitted scalars take their zero values; no interval is defaulted. Only the exact zero value (false, 0) normalizes to absence; false with a positive interval and true with zero interval remain stored. JSON null is not an omitted value.

SensitiveResult.description: Existing internal/core/sensitive_info.go SensitiveResult; no new detector or scoring mechanism.

ContextObservationMeta.description: Contract-only metadata, not a persistence or tenancy claim. epochDigest is a local SHA-256 content binding, not an export identifier. nativeAttemptId/reviewId are vendor associations, never inferred.

ContextObservation.description: #95 S1 contract only: no routes, collector, persistence or retention implementation. OTel payloads remain opt-in; all retained strings use whole-content RedactText omission. Coverage is source-bound, not evidence of provider submission. See context-observation.md.
